summary: Steady dedicated-pool throughput plateau caused by delayed scheduler heartbeats and placement handshakes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated pool report a hard throughput ceiling plateau where p50/p90 remain fine but sustained throughput is ~40% below historical levels despite ample GPUs being shown as Available.

Impact:
- EdgeDocs experiences sustained lower tokens/sec on their dedicated pool during business hours (approx 09:00-18:00 PDT).
- Client traffic is not receiving 429s, calls succeed but tail latency and throughput are depressed, causing backlog on the customer side and increased internal queueing.
- Business impact: degraded user experience for their product search feature; potential SLA breach if not resolved.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-ec-003 (EdgeDocs reserved cluster)
- Region: us-west-2
- Node type: A100-80GB heterogeneous blend (some older A100-40GB in same pool)
- Routing policy: latency-preferring with fallbacks to auto-quantized model variants

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) Run sustained generation workload (many short streams, median context 512 tokens) from EdgeDocs tenant over 30+ minutes.
2) Observe that new allocations are accepted but placement time spikes from ~150ms to ~1200-3000ms intermittently.
3) CPU-side metrics show repeated preemption/handshake events with GPUs where KV cache warmups are happening then evictions re-triggered.
4) Throughput tops out and does not recover even after load stabilizes; pool reports Available GPUs in console but effective throughput remains capped.

Logs & traces (excerpt):
- scheduler.trace: allocation_request -> placement_ack delta: steady increase to 1.2s at plateau windows
- autoscaler.log: "placement_retry=3 backoff=200ms" seen repeatedly for same tenant slices
- serving-runtime: "kv_cache_evict start" logged concurrently with "gpu_handshake_timeout" in multiple pods

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Increased pool reserved capacity by +2 slots (temporary) — transient improvement then reversion to plateau after ~12 minutes.
- Pinned EdgeDocs tenant to a single host to reduce cross-host KV warmups — throughput improved by ~10% but still below baseline.
steps_to_reproduce: Sustain short-stream generation workload at scale for 30+ minutes
Observe placement time and allocation handshakes in scheduler traces
Monitor serving-runtime kv_cache and eviction logs concurrent with placement retries
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy-neighbor or GPU fragmentation. Evidence summary pointed elsewhere: repeated placement handshakes and delayed scheduler heartbeats appearing at the same time window.

Findings so far:
- Scheduler heartbeats to the placement coordinator intermittently delayed by up to 800ms during plateau windows. Heartbeat delay correlated with increased allocation round-trips and placement retries.
- Placement retries cause short-lived preemptions: an in-flight tenant slot is briefly relinquished and reacquired, triggering KV cache eviction/warmup cycles and increasing per-request overhead.
- Autoscaler debounce/backoff parameters allowed multiple near-simultaneous placement attempts for different tenants which amplified slot churn.
- Background GC activity on one older A100 host coincided with the largest heartbeat delays by timestamp correlation.

Hypotheses:
1) Non-deterministic heartbeat jitter from a combination of host-level GC and the scheduler's single-threaded coordinator loop is causing slow placement acknowledgements.
2) Autoscaler debounce settings are too aggressive for short-stream-heavy workloads; parallel placement retries cause unnecessary preemptions and slot churn rather than graceful queuing.
3) KV cache eviction on preemption is expensive enough to reduce effective tokens/sec such that apparent Available GPUs don't translate into usable throughput.

Evidence links: 
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cluster/dedicated-pools?orgId=1&var-pool=dp-ec-003
- Tracing: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/0b8a9c2
- Sample logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/edge/274199/placements.zip
actions_taken:
1) Forced tenant pinning to single host for testing (temporary) — gave ~10% immediate uplift.
2) Bumped scheduler heartbeat frequency temporarily on coordinator in us-west-2 canary — reduced observed heartbeat lag in canary by 60%.
3) Raised autoscaler debounce interval and introduced linear backoff for repeated placement retries in staging to validate impact.
4) Engaged infra to collect host-level metrics on suspected older A100 node for background processes and GC timings.
5) Asked customer to slightly reduce short-stream concurrency as a stopgap (customer accepted temporary throttling).
resolution:
Work in progress: engineering patch prepared to harden scheduler coordinator and change placement retry behavior (PR linked). Planned rollout: canary in staging then gradual roll to us-west-2 dedicated pools.

Target fix details:
- Change scheduler to batch placement acknowledgements and add a small jitter to heartbeat processing loop to avoid synchronized delays.
- Increase autoscaler placement retry backoff and add a max retry cap that funnels excess requests into a queue rather than immediate preemption.
- Improve KV cache eviction policy to defer full eviction on very short preemptions (soft-evict).

Customer-facing mitigation: keep tenant pinned to a smaller host subset until patch deploy. Finance/CS notified of potential SLA credits if plateau persists.

Next steps:
- Deploy patch to staging and run customer workload replay by 2026-03-14.
- If staging looks good, roll canary to 2 nodes in us-west-2 on 2026-03-15 and monitor for 6 business hours.
- Postmortem/learnings to be written to Confluence after root cause confirms.
